CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Maintain proportional retaliation against US tariff threats while preserving space for negotiation. The announced $50B retaliatory tariffs targeting US soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft should proceed as planned, but China should avoid broadening the conflict beyond matching the US scope. Signal willingness to negotiate if the US scales back its Section 301 list.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading of +0.35 reflects a serious but not yet existential situation. The ZTE denial order (Apr 16) is the most alarming development — a 7-year ban on all US-origin technology that ZTE itself said would 'destroy the company' (Bloomberg, Apr 16 2018). This exposes critical dependency on US semiconductors and directly threatens Made in China 2025 tech self-sufficiency goals. However, the major tariff escalations ($50B Section 301 list, China's $50B retaliation) are still proposed, not implemented — the USTR list has a May 22 comment deadline and at least 180 days before final action (WSJ, Apr 4). China's macro economy remains solid with continued growth, and no tariff-related economic damage has materialized yet.

The action score of -0.4 (retaliate, moderate escalation) reflects several factors. First, China has already announced proportional retaliation that strategically targets Trump's political base — soybeans hit farm-belt states where Trump won 8 of 10 top producers (Bloomberg, Apr 4 2018), and China purchases 61% of total US soybean exports ($14B annually). This creates real domestic political pressure on the administration. Second, failing to follow through on announced retaliation would signal weakness and invite further escalation. Third, both sides still have negotiation windows open — Larry Kudlow stated 'I doubt if there'd be any concrete action for several months' (cited in farm policy reporting). Fourth, broadening the conflict beyond proportional response risks triggering a full trade war before China's domestic semiconductor industry can substitute for US supply. The ZTE case proves this dependency is acute. Retaliate to demonstrate resolve and raise US costs, but do not overextend while supply chain vulnerabilities remain exposed.
key_factors: ZTE denial order (Apr 16) — 7-year US tech ban exposes critical semiconductor dependency
Section 301 $50B tariff list proposed but not yet implemented (May 22 comment deadline)
China's $50B retaliation targets US farm belt — soybeans = $14B in exports to China, 61% of US soybean exports
Neither side's major tariffs are in effect; negotiation window still open
US macro healthy (IP rising, consumer sentiment 98), reducing pressure on US to concede
China's tech self-sufficiency goals (Made in China 2025) directly threatened by entity-list actions

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft)
ZTE Corp. — Chinese telecommunications-gear maker — seven-year ban on purchases of crucial American technology needed to keep it competitive
Trump won eight of the 10 states that are the biggest producers of soybeans. China purchases 61% of total US soybean exports and more than 30% of overall US soybean production.
US Industrial Production rising from 101.46 (Dec 2017) to 102.40 (May 2018), economy healthy
Consumer Sentiment at 98.0 (May 2018), down from peak of 101.4 (Mar) but still elevated
